draft.title: Marketing and business objectives
card: Marketing is how a business finds, attracts and keeps customers. The customers it wins and keeps are its customer base.
Sales
the amount of goods or services sold, counted in units or dollars. A larger customer base can lift sales.
Profit
what is left after costs are taken from revenue. More customers can lift profit, but only if the extra revenue is greater than the extra costs.
Market share
the percentage of all sales in a market that one business makes. It can rise when the business wins customers faster than its rivals do.
draft.remember: Marketing builds a customer base, and that can help a business reach its objectives.

a.q: Which objective is measured as a business's percentage of all sales in its market?
opts: Market share
Sales
Profit
Customer base
a.why: Market share compares a business's sales with the sales of the whole market. Sales only counts what the business sells, so it does not show how the business compares with its rivals.
a.clue: Which objective compares the business with its rivals?

b.q: Priya runs a bakery in Ballarat. A social media campaign brings in many new customers, but she gives big discounts to win them. Which statement is most accurate?
opts: Sales may rise, but profit may not if costs rise too
Profit will rise, because sales have risen
Market share will fall, because prices have fallen
Sales will rise, but the customer base will not grow
b.why: Discounts can bring more customers and sales, but they cut the revenue earned on each item. Profit only rises if revenue grows by more than costs, so rising sales alone do not guarantee it.
b.clue: Profit is revenue minus costs, not just sales.

b.best: Sales may rise, but profit may not if costs rise too

problems.detail: The right option is the only one hedged with 'may'. The three wrong options all say 'will', so a student can pick the answer from its wording without knowing the idea.

The scenario's risk to profit is the discount cutting revenue on each sale, which is what the why explains. The right option instead blames costs rising, so the option and the why do not match the scenario's mechanism.

b.q: Priya runs a bakery in Ballarat. A social media campaign brings in many new customers, but she gives big discounts to win them. Which statement is most accurate?
opts: Sales may rise, but discounts may stop profit from rising
Profit may rise, since profit depends only on sales
Market share may fall, as discounts lower her prices
Her customer base may shrink, as she used discounts
b.why: The new customers can lift sales, but each discounted item brings in less revenue. If that revenue does not cover costs, profit may not rise. Profit depends on revenue and costs, not on sales alone.
b.clue: Think about how much each discounted sale earns.
